editorial:
You get dropped into a tense prison story where Naruto is blamed for crimes he never committed, and every day inside Hozukijou feels like a trap. The setup is fun because you watch him deal with harsh guards, strange inmates, and a warden who seems to know more than he lets on. It mixes action, mystery, and a few big laughs, so the mood stays lively even when things get dark.

The fights are energetic, the pacing rarely slows, and the prison setting gives the movie a fresh feel compared with a normal mission. Some twists are easy to guess, and a few side characters do not get much time, but the main story keeps you hooked. If you enjoy Naruto adventures with danger and humor, this one is worth your time. Stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Naruto survives the prison's power drain, uncovers who set him up, and proves he did not commit the murders. The real plan behind the killings is exposed, Mui's scheme is stopped, and Naruto walks free with his name cleared. You also see the prison's dark secret come to light, giving the story a satisfying finish for fans who wanted clear answers.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves anime action with mystery and prison drama.
